assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Reinstating the defect (CONTROL_SEED set back to SHUFFLE_SEED + 1, i.e. 20261018, which is the landed state) leaves the assertion true: measured, the control recall equals draws[1] and differs from draws[0], so the guard does not redden on the regression it was written for.
Reverting the gap judging leaves name rows whose checks carry no question id, so the assertion reddens; demonstrated in negative-control.log as VERIFY_FAIL with EXIT=1 and 19 unjudged of 737.

findings.text: blocking: CONTROL_SEED = 20261018 equals SHUFFLE_SEED + 1, so _control_permutation (ssog-risk-order-run.py:531-535, random.Random(CONTROL_SEED)) reproduces band draw index 1 of the seed set _shuffled_draws builds at ssog-risk-order-run.py:520-528, random.Random(SHUFFLE_SEED + draw); measured on the committed results.json the control recall equals draws[1] on both splits (calibration 0.2576419213973799, validation 0.22580645161290322), so the control point remains a member of the band sample it is tested against, the inside-band assertion at ssog-risk-order-run.py:863 is true for any input, and the comment at ssog-risk-order-run.py:55-58 that the seed lies outside the band's draw range is false. This is the defect the prior review recorded at run.py:700, moved from band draw 0 to band draw 1 rather than removed.

blocking: the guard independent = recall != draws[0] (and the identical predicate at ssog-risk-order-run.py:899 used by verify) excludes only band draw 0, so it verifies non-identity with one member rather than non-membership in the sample and passes on the landed state; it does not fail on the regression it was added to catch, while the manifest and the commit body both claim the control is now independent.
